title: Sherlock Holmes: A Study in Scarlet — Ep 02/14 — "The Science of Deduction"
description:
A Study in Scarlet, Episode 2. Watson has moved into 221B with a man he cannot place, and he decides to find out what Sherlock Holmes actually knows.

Told in Watson's own voice, cut to under three minutes. For days Holmes lies on the sofa and says nothing; then the working fit takes him and the fiddle scrapes half the night. So Watson takes a pencil and writes the man down — chemistry profound, anatomy accurate, astronomy nil, he had never heard of Copernicus — and can find no trade on earth that wants all of it. Then a plainly-dressed man comes up the stair with a letter, and Watson asks him one question too many.

SOURCE
"A Study in Scarlet" by Arthur Conan Doyle, first published 1887. This episode adapts Chapter II, "The Science of Deduction". The book is in the public domain. Full text from Project Gutenberg: https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/244

HOW THIS WAS MADE
Every picture and every voice in this video is generated with AI. The words are adapted from Arthur Conan Doyle's text and edited by a person; the narration is a synthetic voice, not a recording of anyone; no shot is footage of a real person, a real place or a real event. This video is also declared as altered or synthetic content in YouTube's own disclosure field.
